meta.source: Condensed from the back-office training deck (後台教育訓練_en.pptx, 93 slides, three scenarios). Screens are the test back office as of September 2026; staff names, usernames, keys, passwords and server addresses are covered with solid blocks. Labels in 「brackets」 are what the screen says in Chinese.
meta.glossaryLead: The back office speaks Chinese, the training speaks English, and both use jargon. Left: the word the training uses. Middle: what you will see on screen. Right: what it actually means.

sections.title: Start here
sections.blurb: How the back office is laid out, how to tell test from production, the three levels of on/off switch, and the rules that prevent the expensive mistakes.

sections.title: Game management
sections.blurb: Switching games and providers on and off, maintenance windows, adding games by hand, and syncing them from a provider’s API.

sections.title: Reverse provider onboarding
sections.blurb: A game studio connects its games to our platform: we create it, hand over the connection info, let it test in Playground, then switch it to production and sync its games.
sections.flow: Create provider → Hand over connection info → Enable Playground → Watch progress → All green, leave Sandbox → Sync games → Import test

sections.title: Client onboarding
sections.blurb: A client (tenant) connects to our games: we create the tenant and its credential, the client tests itself in Playground until all green, and only then do we issue the production credential.
sections.flow: Create tenant → Create credential → Enable Playground → Client tests to all green → We QA → Production credential, in production

home.title: Every back-office task, one search away
home.lead: The back-office training, condensed for the CS team: every task, every warning, every screen, with the Chinese labels you will actually see. Search for a task, type what the client just told you, or copy a label off the screen.
chips: turn off a game for one client
home.before: Six rules from the training. Each one prevents a mistake that reaches every client or real money. Click one for the full page.

rules.title: Check the address bar first
rules.text: Test and production look identical. The URL is the only way to tell them apart.

rules.title: One client? Use the client’s page
rules.text: Switching a game off on the provider’s game page takes it away from every client.

rules.title: Nothing goes to production before all green
rules.text: Not a studio leaving Sandbox, not a client’s production credential.

rules.title: Never release the safety valve out of habit
rules.text: Ticking it really disables those games, for everyone.

rules.title: Keys and passwords never go in group chats
rules.text: Encrypted email or a password manager, every time.

rules.title: Never test in production
rules.text: All onboarding and testing happens in the test back office.

home.coloursLead: Every onboarding hint in the back office is colour-coded. The colour tells you whose turn it is before you read a word.

colours.name: Red · their move
colours.text: The other side has something to fix. Send them the card or the report.

colours.name: Green · next step
colours.text: This stage is done. Move on to the next one.

glossary.zh: 租戶 (some pages: 營運商 Operator)
glossary.plain: **Our client**: an operator that offers our games to its players.
**One of the client’s sites or brands.** A tenant can have several; each agent gets its own credential.
**A company that makes games** (a game studio).

glossary.zh: Reverse 供應商 · 反串接
glossary.plain: **A game studio that connects to our platform itself**, instead of us connecting to its API.
**The access badge a client uses to connect to our system.** One per agent; a separate one is issued in production.
A reverse provider’s **signing key**. As sensitive as a password.
A reverse provider’s **Playground login key**.
**A practice room** where the other side tests its integration on its own. Exists only in the test environment.
**Test mode, no real money.** The opposite is Production (正式).
**The real thing**: real players, real money. Also the name of the second back office.

glossary.zh: 全綠通過 · 驗收全綠
glossary.plain: **All tests passed.** The only basis for going to production.
The automated test run the studio or client completes in Playground.
The level of an acceptance report where the first failure stopped the run. Everything after it is skipped, not failed.
**What we pay the studio**: its commission as a percentage of the game’s GGR. Type 5 for 5%.
**What we add on top for the client** (our gross margin), set per client.
Gross gaming revenue: what players bet minus what they win back. Both rates above are percentages of it.
A planned period when a game or provider is down. The system starts and ends it automatically.
A sync guard that blocks a sync from disabling too many games at once.
Provider-list column that tells you how a provider’s games arrive: 手動維護 Manual (added by hand), an API sync result, or 反串接 Reverse.
How the client’s player wallet works with ours, set on the credential (e.g. 現金錢包 Cash wallet).
The client’s address that our platform calls, set on the credential.
The card on a tenant’s Overview that lists what is still missing.
Badge on a client’s game list: the game is off platform-wide, so the client’s own switch is locked.

topics.title: Finding your way around
topics.summary: Five menus on the left. Three of them hold almost everything in this manual: Games, Manage and Tenants.
topics.where: Left menu: {Dashboard|儀表板} · {Reports|報表} · {Tenants|租戶} · {Games|遊戲} · {Manage|管理}
asks: I’m new and don’t know where anything is
Where is the provider list, maintenance, or Playground acceptance?

head: Menu
What’s in it
Used for
rows: {Game list|遊戲列表}, {Provider list|遊戲供應商列表}, {Reverse provider list|Reverse 供應商列表}, plus provider social coins and free-spin management
{Maintenance|維護管理}, {Playground acceptance|Playground 驗收管理}, plus admin lists, permissions and the {Operation log|操作紀錄}
{Create new tenant|建立新租戶}, {Tenant list|租戶列表}

steps.t: Most actions start from the **⋮ menu at the end of a row**. On the provider list it holds {Update provider info|更新供應商資訊} and {View games|查看遊戲}.

shot.cap: Provider list with a row’s ⋮ menu open

tips: The top bar shows the clock in **UTC+8** and the language switch ({Traditional Chinese|繁體中文}). Screens in this manual are in Chinese; the English names are the ones the training uses.

topics.title: Test or production? Check the address bar
topics.summary: There are two back offices and they look identical. All onboarding and testing happens in test. Production is only for the last step: issuing production credentials.
asks: Which back office should I be in?
Am I in production right now?
Where do I issue a production credential?
watch: !The two back offices look the same: same menus, same layout, either theme. **Check the URL before you click anything.**

steps.t: **Test environment:** everything. Creating providers and tenants, Playground, acceptance, switching games during onboarding.
**Production environment:** only the final step, [[production-credential|issuing the production credential]] once a client is all green. Production has no Playground.
Tell them apart by the **address bar** and nothing else. The production address differs from the test one; get both from your lead and bookmark them rather than typing them from memory.

shot.cap: Production back office. The host name is covered in this manual.

topics.title: Three levels of on/off switch
topics.summary: A game can be switched off at three levels. Pick the level that matches who should lose it. The wrong level is the most common expensive mistake.
asks: Should I switch off the provider, the game, or the client?
A client says a game disappeared

head: Level
Where
Who loses the game
Guide
rows: {Provider list|遊戲供應商列表} → ⋮ → {Update provider info|更新供應商資訊} → status
Every game of that studio, for every client
That one game, for every client
Tenant → {Game providers|遊戲供應商} tab → {View games|檢視遊戲}

watch: !Switching a game off on the **provider’s game page** when you meant **one client** turns it off for every client.

topics.title: Yellow, red, green: whose move is it
topics.summary: Every onboarding hint in the back office is colour-coded. Read the colour before you read the words.

head: Colour
Means
Examples
rows: **Our move.** Do what the box says.
{Enable Playground|開通 Playground} inside a yellow hint · the yellow “not all green” warning before leaving Sandbox
**Their move.** The other side has something to fix; send them the report.
{Failed|未通過} on a client’s credential · red phases on a studio’s acceptance card
{All green passed|全綠通過} · {Onboarding complete|對接完成}

tips: Grey usually means **nothing has happened yet**: {Never run|從未執行}, {Not enabled|未開通}, or {Skipped|跳過} in a report, which is not a failure.

topics.title: Five things never to do
topics.summary: The training’s closing list. Each one reaches every client, real money, or a credential.

steps.t: Switch a game off on the **provider game page** when you meant **one client**. → [[game-off-one-client]]
Leave Sandbox, or issue a production credential, **before all green**. → [[rp-leave-sandbox]] · [[production-credential]]
Tick {Release safety valve|放行安全閥} **out of habit**. → [[safety-valve]]
Paste credentials or Secret Keys into **group chats**. → [[secret-key]]
**Test in the production environment.** → [[environments]]

topics.title: Practice exercises
topics.summary: The training’s hands-on round. Do these in groups, in the test environment, before touching a real onboarding.
watch: !**Test environment only.** Check the address bar before you start.

steps.t: Add one game and enable it. → [[add-game]], then [[enable-game]]
Create a reverse provider and enable its Playground. → [[rp-create]], then [[rp-playground]]
Create a tenant, all the way to seeing the Playground section on its credential page. → [[create-tenant]], [[tenant-prerequisites]], [[create-credential]]

topics.title: Who to ask when stuck
topics.summary: Escalation contacts for back-office questions and emergencies.
topics.todo: The training closes on a contacts slide (who to ask when stuck, who to call in an emergency), but the names were given in the room, not written on the slide. Add them here.
tips: Until this is filled in: anything that touches production, releasing the safety valve, or forcing a studio out of Sandbox goes to your manager first. The training says so on each of those pages.

topics.title: Enable a game (rate first)
topics.summary: New games start switched off. Enter the provider cost rate first, then flip the status switch on, then check the client’s side is on too.
topics.where: {Games|遊戲} → {Provider list|遊戲供應商列表} → row ⋮ → {View games|查看遊戲}
asks: A new game needs to go live
The game page says games have no cost rate
What does the red “Unset” badge mean?
watch: !**Rate first, switch second.** Enabling a game before entering its rate makes the reports calculate the wrong money.

steps.t: Open the provider list, then the row’s ⋮ menu → {View games|查看遊戲}. This is the provider’s game page.

Turn on {Show unset only|僅顯示未設定} to list only the games with no rate. They carry a red {Unset|未設定} badge in the {Provider cost GGR%|供應商成本 GGR%} column, and a yellow banner counts them: “This provider still has 18 games with no cost rate set”.

shot.cap: Provider game page (ATG), filtered to games without a rate

steps.t: Open the game’s {Update game info|更新遊戲資訊} dialog, enter {Provider cost GGR%|供應商成本 GGR%} and press {Save|儲存}. The rate is the studio’s commission as a percentage of the game’s GGR: **type 5 for 5%**.
Flip the game’s {Status|狀態} switch on. Grey {Disabled|停用} becomes orange {Enabled|啟用}, effective immediately.

pair.cap: Chicken Tour, rate 3.00% already set, still off

steps.t: Then [[check-client-side|check the client’s side is on too]]. Every client has its own switch for each game.

tips: In the same dialog, a yellow note under the free-spin switches says the provider API’s value is authoritative there and the next GameArt free-spin sync may overwrite a manual setting. The rate is what you came for; leave the free-spin switches alone unless told otherwise.

topics.title: Check the client’s side is on
topics.summary: Every client has its own switch for each game. If a game is on at platform level but a client still can’t see it, look here.
topics.where: {Tenants|租戶} → {Tenant list|租戶列表} → tenant → {Game providers|遊戲供應商} tab → {View games|檢視遊戲}
asks: The client says they can’t see a game we enabled
A game is on but missing for one client

steps.t: Open the client’s {Tenant details|租戶詳情} and go to the {Game providers|遊戲供應商} tab.
On the provider’s row, click {View games|檢視遊戲}.
Find the game and check its {Status|狀態} switch. Green {Enabled|啟用} means this client can offer it.

tips: If the switch is locked and shows a red {Disabled by platform|平台已停用} badge, the game is off for everyone. That is fixed on the provider’s game page, not here: see [[game-off]].

This page shows a different rate column, {Our markup GGR%|我方加成 GGR%（毛利）}: what we add on top for this client. Its yellow banner counts games with no **markup** rate ({markup rate|加成率}), where the provider page counts the **cost** rate ({cost rate|成本率}).

topics.title: Disable a game for everyone
topics.summary: Switching a game off on the provider’s game page takes it away from every client, immediately.
topics.where: Provider’s game page: {Provider list|遊戲供應商列表} → ⋮ → {View games|查看遊戲}
asks: A game is broken and must come off everywhere
The provider retired a game
Why is a client’s switch locked?
watch: !This is platform-wide. If only one client should lose the game, use [[game-off-one-client]] instead.

steps.t: On the provider’s game page, flip the game’s {Status|狀態} switch off. Orange {Enabled|啟用} becomes grey {Disabled|停用}.
It takes effect **immediately, for every client**.
On every client’s game list the game now shows a red {Disabled by platform|平台已停用} badge and the client’s switch is **locked**: they cannot turn it back on.

shot.cap: A client’s game list after the platform-wide disable

tips: If the game is only down for a while, use [[maintenance-unplanned|maintenance]] instead of switching it off. Maintenance can end on its own; a switch stays off until someone remembers it.

topics.title: Turn a game off for one client only
topics.summary: Use the client’s own detail page, not the provider’s game page.
topics.where: {Tenants|租戶} → tenant → {Game providers|遊戲供應商} → {View games|檢視遊戲}
asks: One client wants a game removed
Turn off a game for this operator only
watch: !Using the provider game page instead switches the game off for **every** client.

steps.t: Open the client’s {Tenant details|租戶詳情} → {Game providers|遊戲供應商} tab → {View games|檢視遊戲} on the provider’s row.
Flip **this client’s** {Status|狀態} switch off. Only this client loses the game.

shot.cap: Tenant’s game list: a switch here affects this client only

tips: To take a whole provider away from one client, use the {Enabled?|是否開啟} switch on the {Game providers|遊戲供應商} tab itself. See [[provider-off]].

topics.title: Schedule a maintenance window
topics.summary: When a provider announces downtime, create a window. The system starts and ends it automatically.
topics.where: {Manage|管理} → {Maintenance|維護管理} → {Create maintenance window|建立維護視窗}
asks: A provider sent a maintenance notice
A game will be down from 10:00 to 12:30
Planned downtime

steps.t: Go to {Manage|管理} → {Maintenance|維護管理} and press {Create maintenance window|建立維護視窗}.

shot.cap: Maintenance list: one provider in progress, one ended

steps.t: Set the scope, {Maintenance level|維護層級}: {Game|遊戲} or {Provider|供應商}. Pick the targets; for games, one or more in {Target games|目標遊戲}.
Enter {Start time|開始時間} and {End time|結束時間}. Choose the {Source|來源}, {Provider notice|供應商通知} (the default) or {Self-detected|自行偵測}, and add a {Reason|原因}, such as the provider’s notice text.
Press {Confirm|確認}. The system **starts and ends** the window automatically.

tips: End time is optional. Leave it empty and the list shows {No scheduled end time|無預定結束時間}; then someone has to [[maintenance-unplanned|end it by hand]].
The back-office clock runs on UTC+8, and a provider notice quotes its own time zone (the training example says GMT+8). Convert before you type the times.
labels: 開始時間 · 結束時間
供應商通知 · 自行偵測

topics.title: Start or end maintenance now
topics.summary: For unplanned downtime: start maintenance on the spot from the game or provider list, and end it once the problem is fixed.
asks: A game is broken right now
A provider is down unexpectedly
The problem is fixed but the game is still in maintenance

steps.t: Find the game in {Game list|遊戲列表} (or the provider in the provider list) and press {Start maintenance now|立即維護} at the end of its row.

shot.cap: Game list, filtered to one game

steps.t: Once it is fixed, open {Maintenance|維護管理}, find the {In progress|進行中} row, and press {End maintenance|結束維護} in its action cell.

shot.cap: Maintenance list scrolled to the right

tips: Only a window still {In progress|進行中} has an End maintenance button. Ended rows offer the bell (notification results) and a view icon only.
In the provider list, a provider under maintenance carries a blue {Under maintenance|維護中} badge, next to green {Enabled|啟用} and red {Disabled|停用}.

topics.title: Did the maintenance notice reach the client?
topics.summary: Every maintenance window records the notifications sent to clients. Check it, and resend any that failed.
topics.where: {Maintenance|維護管理} → the window’s bell icon → notification results
asks: A client says nobody told them about the maintenance
Did the maintenance notification go out?

steps.t: In {Maintenance|維護管理}, press the **bell** icon at the end of the window’s row. The notification results open under the row.

shot.cap: Notification results, here in its empty state

steps.t: Read the result for each client. If a send **failed**, press **Resend**.

tips: {No data|沒有資料} means no notification was recorded for that window. Read it as “nothing was sent”, not “delivered”.

topics.title: Disable a provider
topics.summary: Turn off a whole studio: for everyone from the provider list, or for one client from that client’s page.
asks: Stop a provider for all clients
One client doesn’t want this provider any more

steps.t: **For everyone:** {Provider list|遊戲供應商列表} → row ⋮ → {Update provider info|更新供應商資訊}. Check the dialog names the right provider ({Editing|編輯對象}), set {Status|狀態} to {Disabled|停用}, and {Save|儲存}.
A {Confirm information|確認資訊} window repeats what will be saved: status, currencies, countries. Read it, then {Confirm|確認}.
**For one client only:** open the client’s {Tenant details|租戶詳情} → {Game providers|遊戲供應商} tab and flip that provider’s {Enabled?|是否開啟} switch off.

tips: A disabled provider shows a red {Disabled|停用} badge in the provider list, with dashes instead of its currency and country counts.

topics.title: Add a game by hand
topics.summary: Providers without an API sync (“Manual” in Last sync) get their games added by hand. A new game starts switched off.
topics.where: Provider’s game page → {Add game|新增遊戲}
asks: The provider sent us a new game but it isn’t in the list
How do I add a game?
watch: !The **game code must match the provider’s exactly**.

steps.t: In the provider list, check the {Last sync|上次同步} column. {Manual|手動維護} means no API sync, so games are added by hand. API providers have an {Update games|更新遊戲} button instead: see [[sync-update-games]].
Open the provider’s game page and press {Add game|新增遊戲}.
Fill in {Name|名稱}, {Game code|遊戲代碼} and {Provider cost GGR%|供應商成本 GGR%}, and upload the logo. The form also has category, status, devices, currency, target market and a demo switch.

lb: Game code: must match the provider

steps.t: {Save|儲存}. A {Created successfully|創建成功} toast confirms it.

shot.cap: Saved; the toast appears top right

steps.t: The new game appears at the end of the list, **switched off**. Take it through [[enable-game]].

tips: The logo upload takes JPG, PNG, GIF, WEBP or SVG, up to 10 files.

topics.title: Sync games from a provider’s API
topics.summary: API-synced providers have an Update games button. It shows a preview first; nothing changes until you confirm.
topics.where: {Provider list|遊戲供應商列表} → {Update games|更新遊戲} on the provider’s row
asks: The provider added new games
Refresh a provider’s game list
What do the sync counts mean?

steps.t: Press {Update games|更新遊戲} on the provider’s row. The row also shows the last result: time, then {Added|新增} · {Fields filled|補欄位} · {Disabled|停用} · {Re-enabled|重啟} · {Errors|異常}, and who ran it.
Read the **preview**. It counts what the sync would do, including {Added|新增}, {Disabled|停用} and {Unchanged|無變更}. The banner says it plainly: this is a preview and nothing has been written yet.

shot.cap: Update games preview: nothing needs to change

steps.t: Press {Confirm and execute|確認執行}. The system fetches the list again and writes it, so the real result can differ from the preview. A green {Sync complete|同步完成} banner shows what actually happened; then {Close|關閉}.

lb: Close (the result is the green banner)
shot.cap: The actual result after Confirm and execute

steps.t: Newly added games arrive **switched off**. Take each one through [[enable-game]] to set its rate.

tips: If the preview would disable many games at once, the [[safety-valve]] holds them back.
Rows reading {Reverse|反串接} have no Update games button; see [[reverse-sync]]. {Not yet synced|尚未同步} means the button has never been used for that provider.
labels: Missing, held by the safety valve
缺漏（被安全閥擋下，不停用）

topics.title: The safety valve
topics.summary: If a sync would disable too many games at once, the system blocks it. Release it only if the provider really retired those games.
asks: The sync says “Safety valve triggered”
Games are listed as Missing in the sync preview
watch: !Releasing the valve **really does disable** those games, for every client. Not sure? Ask your manager.

steps.t: A red {Safety valve triggered|安全閥已觸發} block appears in the Update games preview. In the training example the provider returned **1** game while **6** were active: disabling 5 would exceed the limit (30% of active games, so at most 1 here). The 5 are held under {Missing, held by the safety valve|缺漏（被安全閥擋下，不停用）}.

shot.cap: Update games preview for ATG, valve triggered

steps.t: Ask the provider: did they **really retire** those games, or is their list incomplete? The second case is what the valve is for.

Only if they really retired them: tick {Release safety valve|放行安全閥} at the bottom of the preview, then {Confirm and execute|確認執行}. The help text says it plainly: once ticked, this sync disables the games in the Missing list.

shot.cap: Bottom of the preview; unticked by default

steps.t: Otherwise press {Cancel|取消}. Nothing is written and the games stay on.

topics.title: Sync a reverse provider’s games
topics.summary: Providers whose Last sync reads “Reverse” have no Update games button. Their games are synced from the provider detail page.

steps.t: In the provider list, rows reading {Reverse|反串接} show {Provider detail|供應商詳情} instead of Update games. Press it.
On the detail page, use the {Game list|遊戲列表} card: fetch, review, sync to database. The full steps are in [[rp-sync-games]].

topics.title: The whole flow, start to finish
topics.summary: A game studio connects to our platform itself. We create it, hand over the connection info, open a Playground for it to test in, then switch it to production and sync its games.
asks: A new studio wants to integrate with us
Where is this studio in onboarding?

head: Step
What happens
Whose move
rows: We create it in the test back office. The code is permanent.
Copy the full connection info to the studio’s engineer. The Secret Key goes by a secure channel.
Copy the delivery package (Access Key and URLs) to the studio.
The studio runs acceptance. Red is theirs to fix.
Get the production API URL from the studio, then Disable Sandbox.
Fetch the game list and sync it; then rates and enabling.
Launch, bet and settle on XSINO and HeavenOnline before release.

steps.t: The provider’s detail page tracks the big stages in {Onboarding progress|對接進度}: {Create provider|建立供應商} → {Deliver connection info, enable Playground|交付接入資訊、開通 Playground} → {Provider self-test acceptance|供應商自測驗收} → {Switch to production, go live|切換正式模式上線}. A yellow “next step” hint underneath says what to do now.

shot.cap: Provider detail: steps 1–2 done, step 3 current

topics.title: Create the reverse provider
topics.summary: Enter name, code and currencies. The API URL and IP whitelist can stay empty: the studio’s engineers fill them in later.
topics.where: {Games|遊戲} → {Reverse provider list|Reverse 供應商列表} → {Create Reverse provider|新增 Reverse 供應商}
asks: Set up a new studio in the back office
watch: !The **provider code cannot be changed** after creation ({Cannot be modified after creation|建立後不可修改}). Agree it with the studio first.

steps.t: Open {Reverse provider list|Reverse 供應商列表} and press {Create Reverse provider|新增 Reverse 供應商}.
Enter {Provider name|供應商名稱}, {Provider code|供應商代碼} and {Available currencies|可用貨幣}. Leave {API URL|API URL} and {IP whitelist|IP_WHITELIST} empty unless you already have them.
Create it. The Secret Key appears **once**: read [[secret-key]] before you close that window.

tips: The dialog notes that IP verification is not switched on yet; whitelist settings take effect in a future version.
Existing codes are short and lower-case: rectangle, yeebet, vplus.

topics.title: The Secret Key: copy once, deliver securely
topics.summary: A studio’s Secret Key is as sensitive as a password. Copy it when it appears and deliver it only through a secure channel.
asks: Where do I send the Secret Key?
Can I post the key in the group chat?
The studio needs a new Secret Key
watch: !**Never paste it in a group chat.** Use encrypted email or a password manager.

steps.t: The key is shown in full when the provider is created. (The training screenshot is the **regenerate** window, which looks the same.) {Copy full connection info|複製完整接入資訊} copies the Callback URL, provider code, key and headers in one go.

shot.cap: Secret Key window. Key and URL covered in this manual.

steps.t: Tick {I have copied and safely saved the above|我已複製並安全保存上述資訊}, then {Confirm|確認}.
Deliver it to the studio’s engineer through a **secure channel**: encrypted email or a password manager.

tips: Lost before delivery? {Regenerate Secret Key|重新產生 Secret Key} on the detail page makes a new one, but the **old key stops working immediately** and the studio must switch over. The new key is shown in full only once, so have the delivery channel ready first.

Before regenerating, try {View Secret Key|查看 Secret Key} on the {Credential settings|憑證設定} card. The key window’s own note appears to say the key can be fetched again there without regenerating, but its wording is barely legible in the training screenshot. Confirm with your lead.
The headers block shows what the studio must send with each request: `X-Provider-Code`, `X-Signature` (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with the secret) and `X-Timestamp` (Unix milliseconds).

topics.title: Hand over the connection info
topics.summary: Copy the full connection info from the provider’s detail page and paste it to the studio’s engineer.
topics.where: Reverse provider detail → {Connection info|接入資訊} card
asks: The progress bar is at step one
What do I send the studio’s engineer?

steps.t: The detail page opens on the {Onboarding progress|對接進度} bar: four steps, with a yellow “next step” hint saying what to do now.
Scroll to {Connection info|接入資訊} and press {Copy full connection info|複製完整接入資訊}. Paste it to the studio’s engineer.

Not sure what a field means? Hover the **?** icons for a plain-language explanation. The Sandbox one reads: Sandbox is a test environment and doesn’t touch real money; production is the real connection; keep Sandbox on until acceptance is all green.

topics.title: Enable Playground for a studio
topics.summary: Playground is where the studio tests on its own. It needs the provider to be active and in Sandbox mode.
topics.where: Reverse provider detail → {Playground account|Playground 帳號} card
asks: The Playground card says prerequisites not met
Give the studio its test access

steps.t: On the {Playground account|Playground 帳號} card, check {Enable prerequisites|開通前置條件}: {Credential status is active|憑證狀態為啟用} and {Credential is in Sandbox mode|憑證處於 Sandbox 模式}. A red mark means not met (here the provider is disabled) and the button stays greyed out.

shot.cap: Prerequisites not met: the provider is disabled

steps.t: With both green, press {Enable Playground|開通 Playground}.
An Access Key window opens. Press {Copy full delivery package|複製完整交付包} (Access Key, provider code, Playground URL and Callback URL together) and send it to the studio.

shot.cap: Access Key window. Key and URLs covered.

tips: Closed the window too early? {View Access Key|查看 Access Key} on the account card brings it back. No need to reissue.

topics.title: The studio lost its Access Key
topics.summary: Reissue it from the Playground account card. The old key can no longer sign in.
asks: The studio says they lost the key
The studio can’t log in to Playground

steps.t: First try {View Access Key|查看 Access Key}. If the key is still on record, resend it without reissuing.
Otherwise press {Reissue Access Key|重發 Access Key} on the {Playground account|Playground 帳號} card and send the new key in [[rp-playground|the delivery package]].
Warn the studio that the **old key is dead** for new sign-ins.

tips: Reissuing does not end a Playground session that is already logged in (sessions last 24 hours). It only stops the old key from signing in again.

topics.title: Watch a studio’s test progress
topics.summary: The Acceptance status card shows passed and failed counts phase by phase. The full curriculum verdict is the summary.
topics.where: Reverse provider detail → {Acceptance status|驗收狀態}
asks: How far along is the studio?
There’s red in the acceptance status
Which studios are still in Sandbox?

steps.t: Open the {Acceptance status|驗收狀態} card. Each phase shows passed, failed, warning and skipped counts: {Integration setup|整合設定}, {Signature|簽名}, {Game list|遊戲列表}, {Launch game|啟動遊戲}, {Wallet gates M1–M8|錢包關卡}, Freespin, {Reconciliation|對帳}. {Full curriculum verdict|完整課綱判定} at the bottom is the summary.

For every studio at once, use the {Reverse provider list|Reverse 供應商列表}: the {Sandbox mode|Sandbox 模式} column (Sandbox or {Production|正式}) and the {Playground account|Playground 帳號} column ({Enabled|已開通} or {Not yet enabled|尚未開通}).

shot.cap: Reverse provider list: every studio’s stage on one page

steps.t: **Red is theirs to fix.** Send the studio the card. Nothing is needed from us until it is all green.

tips: Until it is ready, a yellow summary counts what is left, for example “3 items left before switching to production: no test game selected, 5 test phases and 8 wallet gates not passed”.
A phase in orange **warning**, such as skipped checks in Launch game, can still sit under a Passed verdict. The verdict is what counts.

topics.title: All green: switch the studio to production
topics.summary: Once acceptance is all green, get the production API URL from the studio and disable Sandbox.
topics.where: Reverse provider detail → {Connection info|接入資訊} → {Disable Sandbox|關閉 Sandbox}
asks: Acceptance is all green, what now?
The system warns acceptance isn’t all green when switching
watch: !Without all green the system shows a **yellow warning** but still lets you switch. **Don’t force it** without asking your manager.

steps.t: Confirm the {Acceptance status|驗收狀態} card is **all green**. Check it yourself.
Get the **production API URL** from the studio.
On {Connection info|接入資訊}, press {Disable Sandbox|關閉 Sandbox}.

Replace the {Production API URL|正式 API URL}. It may still hold the sandbox address the studio typed during testing, and after the switch **players’ game launches go straight to this address**. Then {Switch to production mode|切換為正式模式}.

shot.cap: Switch dialog: top on the left, bottom on the right with the not-all-green warning

steps.t: All four progress steps are ticked and a green banner reads {This provider has switched to production; onboarding complete|此供應商已切換正式模式，對接完成。}.

tips: A ticked last step does **not** prove acceptance passed: the system allows the switch before all green. Check the acceptance card, not the progress bar.
Forcing the switch does not make Freespin usable. Freespin still needs a valid Phase 4 verification, and the client’s credential must also be authorised for it.

topics.title: Sync a studio’s games to our platform
topics.summary: Fetch the studio’s game list on its detail page, review the preview, then sync to database. New games arrive switched off.
topics.where: Reverse provider detail → {Game list|遊戲列表} card
asks: Onboarding is complete, how do the games get in?
The studio added games

steps.t: On the {Game list|遊戲列表} card, fetch the list ({Re-fetch|重新拉取}) and review the preview table. A blue banner says it is preview data, not yet synced.

shot.cap: Game list card: 25 games in preview

steps.t: Press {Sync to database|同步至資料庫} and confirm: “About to sync 25 games to the database. New games default to disabled. Continue?”
A green banner reports the result, e.g. “Sync complete. 4 added, 21 updated”, and reminds you new games are disabled: set their rates and enable them on the game management page.
Take each new game through [[enable-game]]: rate first, then the switch. Then the [[rp-import-test|import test]].

topics.title: Import test before release
topics.summary: Before clients get a new studio’s games, prove they work on our own platforms.

steps.t: Import the games on our **XSINO** and **HeavenOnline** platforms.
Confirm each one **launches, accepts bets, and settles**.
**Release to clients only after the test passes.**

topics.title: The whole flow, start to finish
topics.summary: A client (tenant) connects to our games. We create it and its credential in test, the client tests itself in Playground until all green, we check, and only then do we issue the production credential, in production.
asks: A new client is signing on
Where is this client in onboarding?

head: Step
What happens
Whose move
rows: Name, time zone, currencies. Confirm the time zone with the client.
A tenant user and an agent, until the health dashboard is clear.
Wallet mode, webhook URL, IP whitelist. Then [[deliver-credential|deliver it]].
Copy the login info to the client before closing the window.
The client runs acceptance L0–L5. Red is theirs to fix.
In the production back office, only after all green.

topics.title: Create the tenant
topics.summary: Only the brand name is needed to create it; time zone, language and status come pre-filled. Check the time zone with the client before saving.
topics.where: {Tenants|租戶} → {Create new tenant|建立新租戶}
asks: Set up a new client
Which time zone should the client have?
watch: !The **time zone sets the daily cut-off in reports**. It defaults to UTC+0: confirm it with the client.

steps.t: Open {Tenants|租戶} → {Create new tenant|建立新租戶}.
Enter {Name|名稱} (the brand name) and set {Time zone|時區}, {Language|語言} and {Currency|貨幣}.

lb: Time zone: confirm with the client

steps.t: Save. Optional fields (target market, {Licence|憑證} such as Curaçao, {Role|角色} such as Whitelabel) can be added later with Edit.

tips: {Required|必填}: name, time zone, language, status. Defaults: UTC+0, English, Enabled. {Optional|選填}: target market, currency, licence, role.

topics.title: Complete the tenant’s prerequisites
topics.summary: The health dashboard on the tenant’s Overview lists what is missing. Create a tenant user and an agent; the agent’s API keys turn Ready once its credential exists.
topics.where: Tenant detail → {Overview|總覽} → {Health dashboard|健康度儀表板}
asks: Red text on the tenant’s health card
The agent’s API keys say Missing

steps.t: On {Overview|總覽}, the {Health dashboard|健康度儀表板} lists what still needs doing under {Needs attention|需要處理}, for example “agent user missing”. {Go to fix|前往處理} jumps to the right place.

shot.cap: Tenant overview with the health dashboard

steps.t: {Tenant users|租戶使用者} tab → {Create|創建}: name and status. The password is generated for you. **Copy it first**: it can’t be viewed again once you leave the page.
{Agents|代理商} tab → {Add agent|新增代理商}: name and status, then {Create|創建}.

In the agent list, the {API keys|API 金鑰} column starts at orange {Not created|未建立} (the training calls it “Missing”). It turns green {Created|已建立} (“Ready”) once [[create-credential|the credential]] exists.

pair.cap: The same agent after its credential was made

tips: The tiles at the top count agents, tenant users, API keys (ready / total) and providers.

topics.title: Create the client’s credential
topics.summary: Each agent gets an API credential: choose the wallet mode and enter the client’s webhook URL. Once it exists, the Playground section appears on the credential page.
topics.where: Tenant detail → {Agents|代理商} → the agent’s Credential button
asks: The credential page is empty
Where do I put the client’s webhook URL and IPs?

steps.t: In the agent list, press the agent’s **Credential** button (one of the icons on its row). An empty page says {No API credential created yet|尚未創建API憑證}. Press {Go to create|前往創建}.
Fill in {Webhook URL|Webhook 網址}, {Status|狀態}, {Wallet mode|錢包模式} (e.g. {Cash wallet|現金錢包}) and the client’s {IP whitelist|白名單IP} (several IPs separated by commas), then {Create|創建}.

shot.cap: Add agent API credential, with example values

steps.t: The {Wallet Acceptance Playground|Wallet 驗收 Playground} section now appears at the top of the credential page, in the test environment only.

shot.cap: Credential page: Playground section, not enabled yet

tips: Pick the wallet mode the client integrated against. Only {Cash wallet|現金錢包} appears in the training; ask if the client mentions anything else.

topics.title: Deliver the credential
topics.summary: Email the credential to your own work inbox (or copy it), then pass it to the client.
topics.where: Credential page → {Send API credential notification|發送API憑證通知}
asks: How does the client get its credential?

steps.t: On the credential page, open {Send API credential notification|發送API憑證通知}. Add **your own work email** under {Recipients|收件人} with {Add|新增}, then {Send|發送}. Or copy the credential instead.
Deliver it to the client.

tips: The client back office isn’t ready yet, so **operations staff** currently handle delivery.
Recipients can also be picked from the tenant’s users, agent users or saved contacts. The training sends to your own inbox first.

topics.title: Enable Playground for a client
topics.summary: One click generates the client’s Playground login. Copy the login info before closing: the password is shown only once.
topics.where: Credential page → yellow hint → {Enable Playground|開通 Playground}
asks: The client needs its test login
Yellow box in the progress section
Grey “Not enabled”

steps.t: The yellow hint on the credential page reads: “Next step: press Enable Playground to generate the login account, then hand the URL, account and initial password to the client together.” Press {Enable Playground|開通 Playground} inside it.
Confirm. The username is generated automatically (tenant + agent + random code). The initial password is generated and shown once; the client must change it at first login.
In the {Account created|帳號已建立} window, press {Copy login info|複製登入資訊} **before** {Confirm|確認}.

shot.cap: Account created. URL, username and password covered.

steps.t: Paste the four lines (URL, Operator, Username, Password) to the client as they are.

shot.cap: The copied lines in a notepad, password masked

tips: The initial password can be delivered again later only if it was saved, the client hasn’t changed it, and you have reset-password permission. It is masked by default.

topics.title: The client hasn’t started testing
topics.summary: “Never run” means the account exists but the client hasn’t run acceptance. Copy the connection info and remind them.
asks: The client hasn’t tested yet
The client lost the Playground password
The client changed the password and needs it again
The client can’t log in

steps.t: The badge reads {Never run|從未執行}. Press {Copy connection info|複製接入資訊} and send it as a reminder to log in and run the full L0–L5 verification. Until it is all green, nothing is needed from us.
If an initial password is still available, a **Password** line follows Username in what you copy. Otherwise the copy is three lines.
If {Initial password|初始密碼} reads {Changed by the client; reset required for redelivery|客戶已自行變更，需重設密碼方可再交付。}, the client set their own. **Reset only when needed**: {Reset password|重設密碼}.

shot.cap: Initial password already changed by the client

tips: The account block also shows {Lock status|鎖定狀態}, the count of failed logins. Look there first when a client says they can’t log in.

topics.title: The client says it’s done: check the colour
topics.summary: Don’t take their word for it. Red “Failed” means not done: send the report. Green “All green” means QA passed.
topics.where: Credential page → the Playground section’s badge
asks: The client says testing is finished
The client says they passed

steps.t: Red {Failed|未通過}: not done. The hint counts the failing cases (e.g. 6 of 69) and says not to create the production credential until all green. Press {View report|檢視報告} and send it to the client’s engineer.

shot.cap: Credential page: the latest run failed

steps.t: Green {All green passed|全綠通過}: QA passed. The hint says to go to the **production** back office and create the production credential. Playground exists only in test, so there is nothing more to do here.

topics.title: Read an acceptance report
topics.summary: Top half: who and what was tested. Bottom half: which level failed. Fix the blocking level first.
topics.where: Credential page → {View report|檢視報告}, or {Manage|管理} → {Playground acceptance|Playground 驗收管理}
asks: What does this report mean?
The report is full of grey Skipped
The client asks why it failed

steps.t: **Top half:** status label, counts, and the test details: test player, currency, test game, start and end time. Compare them with what the client told you.
**Bottom half:** levels L0, L1 and onward, each with passed, failed and skipped counts. The level tagged {Blocking level|阻塞層} is where a failure stopped the run. **Fix that first.**
Expand a failed case to see the {Failure reason|失敗原因}, the request we sent and the client’s response. That is what their engineer needs.

tips: Grey {Skipped|跳過} is **not** a failure: an earlier failure blocked it. Fix the failures, re-run, and the skipped cases will run.
In the training example every L0 case took about 10 seconds and the response was an i/o timeout: the client’s server never answered our request. That is on their side.

topics.title: Every client’s test status on one page
topics.summary: Playground acceptance lists every client credential with a colour-coded status. Use it to find who is stuck.
topics.where: {Manage|管理} → {Playground acceptance|Playground 驗收管理}
asks: Which clients are stuck in testing?
What does each status mean?

steps.t: Open {Playground acceptance|Playground 驗收管理}. Filter by {Verification status|驗證狀態} or search by keyword.

shot.cap: Playground acceptance. Usernames and keys covered.

head: Status
Means
What to do
rows: No Playground account for this credential yet.
Open the credential page and [[client-playground|enable it]].
The account exists; the client hasn’t run the test.
Wait for it to finish before reading anything.
Interrupted, by a timeout or a manual stop.
Ask the client to run it again.

tips: This page is for looking only. Enabling, password resets, unlocking and disabling all happen on the credential page.

topics.title: Issue the production credential
topics.summary: Only after all green. Log in to the production back office, repeat create tenant and create credential there, then deliver it.
topics.where: The **production** back office
asks: The client is all green, what now?
How does a client go live?
watch: !**Never issue a production credential before all green.**

steps.t: Log in to the **production** back office, and check the address bar.
Repeat [[create-tenant]] and [[create-credential]] in production.
It is the same credential form as in test. **Production has no Playground section, and that is expected.**
Email the credential to your own work inbox or copy it, then deliver it to the client, with the same {Send API credential notification|發送API憑證通知} flow.

shot.cap: The same send flow in production

situations.see: Not sure if you’re in test or production
situations.do: Look at the address bar. Nothing else on screen tells them apart.

situations.see: Not sure which switch to use
situations.do: Provider = whole studio for everyone · game page = one game for everyone · client’s page = that client only.

situations.see: A new game needs to go live
situations.do: Provider game page → set the rate → switch on → check the client’s side.

situations.see: Red {Unset|未設定} badge in the rate column
situations.do: Enter the provider cost rate before switching the game on.

situations.see: The client says they can’t see a game we enabled
situations.do: Tenant → Game providers → View games: check the client-side switch.

situations.see: Disable a game for everyone
situations.do: Provider game page → switch off. Effective immediately for every client.

situations.see: The client’s switch is locked with {Disabled by platform|平台已停用}
situations.do: The game is off platform-wide. Only the provider game page can turn it back on.

situations.see: One client wants a game removed
situations.do: Client detail → Game providers → View games → switch off. Never the provider game page.

situations.see: A provider announced scheduled downtime
situations.do: Manage → Maintenance → Create maintenance window.

situations.see: A game or provider is broken right now
situations.do: {Start maintenance now|立即維護} on its row; {End maintenance|結束維護} once fixed.

situations.see: A client says they weren’t told about maintenance
situations.do: Maintenance → bell icon on the window → check results, resend on failure.

situations.see: Disable a provider
situations.do: Provider list → ⋮ → Update provider info → Disabled. One client only: their Game providers tab.

situations.see: Add a game by hand
situations.do: Provider game page → {Add game|新增遊戲}. The game code must match the provider’s.

situations.see: A provider added games (API provider)
situations.do: Provider list → {Update games|更新遊戲} → read the preview → Confirm and execute.

situations.see: The sync says {Safety valve triggered|安全閥已觸發}
situations.do: Ask the provider first. Release only if they really retired those games.

situations.see: Provider row says {Reverse|反串接}, no Update games button
situations.do: {Provider detail|供應商詳情} → Game list card.

situations.see: Progress bar at step one
situations.do: Complete the connection info and copy it to the studio.

situations.see: Playground card: {Prerequisites not met|前置條件未滿足}
situations.do: Check the provider is active and in Sandbox.

situations.see: Red in the studio’s acceptance status
situations.do: Theirs to fix. Send them the card.

situations.see: Acceptance status all green
situations.do: Get the production URL from the studio, then Disable Sandbox.

situations.see: Yellow “not all green” warning when switching to production
situations.do: Stop. Don’t force it without your manager.

situations.see: Progress bar says onboarding complete
situations.do: Fetch games, sync to database, then the import test.

situations.see: The studio says the key is lost
situations.do: Try View Access Key first; otherwise reissue and warn them the old one dies.

situations.see: The studio asks for the Secret Key in a group chat
situations.do: Never. Encrypted email or a password manager.

situations.see: Red text on the tenant’s health card
situations.do: Add the tenant user or agent it names.

situations.see: Agent shows API keys {Not created|未建立} (“Missing”)
situations.do: Open the agent’s credential page and create the credential.

situations.see: Empty credential page
situations.do: {Go to create|前往創建}.

situations.see: Yellow box in the progress section
situations.do: Do what the box says.

situations.see: Grey {Not enabled|未開通}
situations.do: Enable Playground.

situations.see: {Never run|從未執行}: the client hasn’t started
situations.do: Copy connection info and chase.

situations.see: The client lost or changed the Playground password
situations.do: Reset the password only when needed, then resend.

situations.see: The client says testing is done
situations.do: Check the colour before believing it.

situations.see: Red {Failed|未通過}
situations.do: Send the report to the client’s engineer.

situations.see: A report full of grey {Skipped|跳過}
situations.do: Not failures. Fix the blocking level and re-run.

situations.see: Green {All green passed|全綠通過}
situations.do: Issue the production credential, in production.
